analyzed_vuln.description: `template_sanity_check` dereferences `fi->file->path.value[...]` / `ffi->file->path.value[...]` based only on `path.len >= 2`, but does not validate that `path.value` points to valid persistent path storage. With malformed profile/template input, file path metadata can become inconsistent (nonzero len with invalid/stale pointer), and the check reads through that pointer. The ASan report shows this becomes a stack-use-after-return read (pointer into prior stack frame, observed via logging frame), so the crash is caused by trusting corrupted path pointer/length pairs during template ID comparison.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `fuzz_pkcs15init`, attacker-controlled profile text is parsed via `process_conf -> process_block -> process_tmpl`. The PoV creates malformed nested template/file entries so a template EF path ends up with an invalid `sc_path` backing pointer while len remains >=2. `process_tmpl` then calls `template_sanity_check`, which computes file IDs from the last two bytes of each path and performs out-of-lifetime memory reads, triggering ASan stack-use-after-return.
